summary: ASTROCARE is a browser-based astronaut health monitoring prototype designed to support health awareness during space missions. Long-duration spaceflight can affect cardiovascular health, bone and muscle function, sleep, mental well-being and other physiological systems. ASTROCARE brings selected health indicators together in a mission-focused dashboard, presents historical NASA spaceflight research data, and provides clearly labelled demonstration readings and rule-based alerts. By combining health-data visualisation, historical research context and an accessible interface, ASTROCARE explores how astronauts could review health information and recognise indicators that may require further attention. It is an independent educational prototype, not a clinically validated medical system.
details:
ASTROCARE – Astronaut Health Monitoring System

The Problem

Long-duration space missions expose astronauts to challenging environmental and physiological conditions, including microgravity, radiation, isolation, confinement and altered sleep cycles. These conditions can influence cardiovascular function, bone and muscle health, immune responses, sleep quality and psychological well-being.

During extended missions, astronauts may have to take greater responsibility for observing changes in their own health. Reviewing different health indicators and understanding their trends can be challenging when information is spread across multiple sources.

Our Solution

ASTROCARE is a browser-based health monitoring prototype that brings selected health information into a mission-focused dashboard. It explores how astronauts could review health indicators, understand historical research data and identify readings that may require attention.

Key Features

  • Mission Overview: A central dashboard presenting the application's health-monitoring information.
  • Vital Signs: A dedicated view for selected physiological indicators.
  • Cardiovascular Monitoring: A section for reviewing cardiovascular-related information.
  • Bone and Muscle Health: A section focused on musculoskeletal health awareness.
  • Sleep and Fatigue: A section for presenting sleep and fatigue-related information.
  • Mental Wellness: A dedicated area for mental well-being awareness.
  • Radiation Tracker: A section for presenting radiation-related information.
  • Alert Centre: Displays alerts based on configured rules and demonstration readings.
  • Health History: Supports reviewing stored health information and trends.
  • Settings: Provides access to application preferences.

The application includes demonstration readings that are explicitly identified as simulated data. These readings are not actual live astronaut telemetry.

NASA Research Data Integration

ASTROCARE incorporates a processed subset of Complete Blood Count (CBC) research data associated with NASA Open Science Data Repository study OSD-569, concerning whole-blood measurements from the SpaceX Inspiration4 mission.

The data provide historical research context for exploring blood-related health indicators. They are not live measurements from astronauts currently in space and should not be interpreted as a real-time operational health feed.

The original NASA study and its associated research information are cited in the project's dataset documentation and references.

Alerting Approach

The prototype uses transparent, configurable rule-based conditions to demonstrate how readings may be flagged for review. These alerts are illustrative and are not medically validated risk predictions, clinical diagnoses or autonomous medical recommendations.

Technology

  • HTML for the application structure.
  • CSS for the user interface and responsive presentation.
  • JavaScript for application behaviour and data handling.
  • Browser-based storage for supported local application data.
  • GitHub Pages for public web deployment.

Potential Impact

ASTROCARE demonstrates how health information from different monitoring areas could be presented in one accessible interface. It aims to support health awareness, make historical research information easier to explore and provide a foundation for future development of astronaut-centred health monitoring tools.

Limitations and Future Development

ASTROCARE is an educational prototype. It is not a medical device and has not undergone clinical validation or operational testing for spaceflight. Demonstration readings are simulated, historical NASA research data are not live telemetry, and the rule-based alerts are illustrative.

Future development could explore integration with validated wearable sensors, additional authorised spaceflight datasets, secure communication systems, individual health baselines and expert-reviewed alert thresholds.

Disclaimer

ASTROCARE is an independent student project. It is not affiliated with, sponsored by, reviewed by or endorsed by NASA. It must not be used as a substitute for professional medical evaluation or mission medical procedures.
